title: node-attribute-synthesis-and-regional-controlplane-notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note on an approach for a regional control-plane-friendly node attribute synthesis layer that sits between telemetry ingestion and routing decisions. Intention is to reduce noisy label churn, enable fast routing decisions across regions, and produce a compact, conflict-resilient node capability index for the inference routing layer.

Context and motivations:
- We need a single authoritative source for per-node capabilities (GPU type, memory, NVLink topology hints, driver/OS version) that is inexpensive to read for routing and can be synced cross-region with bounded staleness.
- Current approach (raw telemetry + ad-hoc labels) causes inconsistent routing decisions during scale events — e.g., transient driver glitches flip "compatible" flags and cause cascading fallbacks.
- Multi-region routing requires predictable fallbacks: prefer local compatible nodes, then warm-fallback region, then global. Control plane must express both hard constraints (e.g., GPU model compatibility) and soft signals (latency/cost preference).

High-level design (synthesis layer):
1) Ingest layer: region-local telemetry collectors push raw signals to a write-ahead buffer: heartbeat, nvlink-topo, pci_ids, gpu_mem_total, gpu_mem_free_est, recent_error_count, temperature, cuda_driver_version. Collector tags signals with source and monotonic timestamp.

2) Synthesis worker (per-region):
- Runs deterministic reconciliation every N seconds (configurable; default 15s).
- Produces a single canonical attribute blob per node: attributes are small, typed key-values with confidence and last_observed. Example keys: gpu.family = "A100x40", gpu.cuda = "12.1.0", gpu.vram_gb = "40", gpu.topology = "NVLink2-n2", node.class = "batch-gpu", node.zone_score = "0.87".
- Each attribute also carries a "source_score" (0..1) and an "aging" TTL. The synth step blends sources and applies rule overrides from operator-managed policies.

3) Health scoring: produce a single health_score in 0..100 computed from weighted signals:
   health_score = 100 - clamp( w_err*err_norm + w_temp*temp_norm + w_mem*mem_pressure + w_p95lat*lat_norm, 0, 100 )
   where weights: w_err=0.35, w_temp=0.2, w_mem=0.25, w_p95lat=0.2 (defaults, operator tunable).
- The worker emits both raw metrics and the synthesized health_score. Health states are mapped to enums: healthy (80+), degraded (50-79), emergency (<50).

4) Capability compatibility fingerprint: for routing we publish a short fingerprint string that encodes the minimal compatibility set (arch:fp). Example: "a100-40-ptx12.1-v2". Fingerprints are computed deterministically from canonical attributes and pinned in the regional index.

Consistency and cross-region sync:
- Regions run their own synthesis workers and maintain a local index for low-latency reads. A global ledger (eventually consistent) syncs fingerprints + last_seen + health_score every 30s using append-only change batches.
- Use conflict-free CRDT-like merge for non-authoritative fields (e.g., last_seen) and authoritative tombstones for removals.
- To avoid flapping, last-good-state is kept for 300s after health drops below threshold before marking as offline globally (operator-configurable). This reduces routing oscillation on transient blips.

Routing policy primitives (for runtime router):
- hard_requirements: list of fingerprint tokens that must match (e.g., arch == a100 and cuda >= 12.0)
- soft_preferences: weighted signals (latency_est, cost_est, health_score, region_preference)
- topology_constraints: prefer same-availability-zone or same-region within X ms budget
- fallback_chain: ordered regions to consider (local -> warm -> global) with per-step capacity fraction and timeout

Example policy pseudocode:
  candidates = index.lookup(hard_requirements)
  candidates = filter(candidates, health_score >= 50)
  scored = score_candidates(candidates, soft_preferences_weights)
  pick = select_best(scored, capacity_budget, spot_burst_allowed)
  if pick == null then goto next_region_in_fallback

Edge cases and heuristics:
- Half-formed telemetry: when collector reports pci_ids but no driver version, assign attribute "cuda": "unknown" with source_score=0.4; matcher treats unknown as wildcard only if policy allows.
- GPU preemption: if a node reports runtime_preemptions > 0 in last 60s, apply sticky penalty to health_score for 10 minutes.
- Heterogeneous multi-GPU nodes: publish per-GPU sub-capabilities (gpu:0, gpu:1). Router can request per-GPU allocation when the model requires split placement. This is heavier weight; default routing will treat node-level minimal capability.

Index format and size estimations:
- Stored per-region as compact rows: node_id, fingerprint, health_score, last_seen, zone, capacity_units, tags[] -> estimated 200 bytes/row.
- For 100k nodes per region, index ~20MB plus telemetry ring buffers. Good for in-memory caches on routing tier.

Operator policies and overrides:
- Operators must be able to pin nodes to a policy (e.g., "vip":true) which bypasses some soft filters. Pins are stored in control-plane DB and are authoritative (overrides synth).
- Rollout instrumentation: when changing weights (health weight, fallback timeouts) enable A/B on a small fleet and observe routing churn metrics (route_success_rate, fallback_rate, cold_start_tokens).

Observability and debug UX:
- Provide a /node/:id/debug endpoint returning: last 10 telemetry samples, synthesized attributes, health_score history, fingerprint, and recent routing decisions that used the node.
- Add a "why-not-picked" trace on routing calls listing top rejection reasons and approximate delta to pass threshold. Helpful for oncall.

Migration plan (from current system):
1) Deploy regional synthesis workers in canary region behind feature flag. Start with read-only synth and emit synthesized blobs to operators only.
2) Enable router to read synth index for sampling (mirror traffic, no cutover). Collect comparison metrics between old and new decisions.
3) Flip traffic for non-critical models, monitor fallback and latency.
4) Gradually expand to critical models with PV tests.

Open questions / TODOs:
- TTL tuning for various attribute types: how long should driver version be authoritative vs transient metrics? Suggestion: static attributes 24h, semi-static 1h, telemetry 30s. Need experiments.
- Do we want push-based notification from synth to router for immediate invalidation (webhook) vs pull-based polling? Tradeoffs: push reduces time-to-react but increases control-plane coupling and ordering complexity.
- Compression of fingerprints for routing lookups: short deterministic integer mapping vs string fingerprint. Need to benchmark memory and CPU tradeoffs.
- Security: ensure synthesized attributes cannot be spoofed by node agents — signing/attestation story required for Private deployments.

Notes to self and next steps:
- Prototype synth worker in go (reuse existing telemetry parsers). Keep API: /synth/v1/node/:id and /synth/v1/index/region/:r/lookup?fp=
- Create experiment plan JIRA JIRA-PLAT-981 and add owners for metric collection: Miguel (telemetry), Priya (router), Samir (ops).
- Prepare short demo for infra weekly: show routing calmness improvement during simulated driver flapping.

References and links:
- Existing node inventory proto: github.com/redwood-inference/node-inventory-proto
- Prior playbook on health-score: shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/node-telemetry-semantic-index-and-routing-guidelines.json

Unresolved decisions marked with [QUESTION] throughout the doc.

-- End of notes --
